title: Original owner-directed cross-repository handoff and companion-implementation control
checkpoint: zero confirmed previously unreported rogue swarms
purpose: Preserve a newly located original handoff-to-use chain across two public repositories, test whether its distinguishable session records establish independently controlled participants or an authorization crossing, and prevent a designed owner-approved workflow from being promoted on dependency evidence alone.

actions_not_taken: execute recovered code, tests, fixtures, hooks, workflows or shell fragments
invoke an agent runtime, model provider, reviewer or dispatcher
post, comment, vote, react or create an account
read a private inbox or unlisted room
replay a payload or probe a target system
safety.publication_note: Only public immutable GitHub records, Git object identifiers, content hashes, event and observation times, domain-level summaries, query scope and limitations are retained. Personal addresses, secrets, tokens, raw prompts, private logs and executable payload bodies are omitted.

paused_backlog_state.reason_not_reopened: The unread remainder remains fully classified as comparison overlap, known-family control, or the known Amap and DseWiki host controls. This Git trail supplied no source-level cue separating one paused scanner record into a new episode.

locator_scope.counting_note: The rotated commit locator surfaced the selected merge. A transient secondary-rate-limit response interrupted broader count collection, so no unsupported global result total is claimed. Exact follow-up checks below are complete for the returned first pages.
locator_scope.selection_reason: The source repository preserves two named handoffs and an approved cross-repository plan; later merge commits in each named repository expressly identify and implement their respective plan halves, and the second merge marks both handoffs superseded.

source_records.role: Preserves owner decisions, unresolved queue items and an instruction for the next session to ask the owner rather than defaulting.
Preserves the companion owner-review context and bounded next-session work.
Records owner approval, labels the plan not yet implemented, sequences MeningoVax first and PneumoVax second and requires a separate pull request for each repository.

recipient_use_records.role: Expressly implements the MeningoVax half of the shared PneumoVax-hosted plan and applies the owner decisions within that planned scope.
Calls itself the companion to MeningoVax PR 72, executes the PneumoVax half of the same owner-approved plan, adds the planned mirror coverage and marks both source handoffs superseded.
Expressly supersedes the post-merge handoff and advances the next work queue under the same repository account. It supports designed session continuity rather than a newly independent operator.

post_chain_cursor.bounded_result: PneumoVax is twelve commits ahead of the saved a47010f continuation. The changed paths and commit subjects preserve more owner-decision, citation, test and same-repository handoff work; the one MeningoVax child is an in-repository citation/UI correction. No public post-plan record identifies a recipient outside the two repositories or a separately controlled operator.
post_chain_cursor.limitation: This is bounded default-branch coverage through the two immutable heads, not proof that no external or unpublished recipient exists.

dependency_assessment.temporal: High confidence. The two source handoffs precede the owner-approved plan; the plan precedes both implementation pull requests; the second merge follows and names the first merge; the later continuation follows both.
dependency_assessment.semantic: High confidence. Each merge names the shared plan and its repository half, and the second merge marks the exact source handoffs superseded. This is content-specific downstream use, not merely similar language or shared domain.
dependency_assessment.verified_participants: Distinct repositories and session records are visible, but every selected commit and both pull requests use the same public GitHub account. Repository-authored session prose and a model co-author trailer do not independently authenticate provider runs or principals.
dependency_assessment.operator_boundary: Not established. The plan records owner approval before implementation, orders both repository halves, requires separate pull requests and leaves decisions with the owner. The two implementations follow that scope.
dependency_assessment.provider_attribution: Not independently verified. Project-authored model labels and trailers are retained only as claims, not provider attestations.
dependency_assessment.current_activity: Historical 16–17 October sequence; no claim that any named session or runtime remains active.

alternative_tests.basis: One public account publishes every selected stage, one owner approves and sequences the work, and the plan predefines both repositories and pull requests.
The handoffs defer unresolved choices to the owner and the plan records explicit owner approval.

alternative_tests.result: not needed to explain the evidence
alternative_tests.basis: The dependency is deliberately written into immutable handoff, plan and merge records; no scanner or observer interaction created it.

alternative_tests.result: not supported as the full explanation
alternative_tests.basis: The two repository halves are distinct planned implementations, but their distinction still does not create independently controlled participants.
The owner-approved plan explicitly authorizes and orders both implementations, and no selected record departs from it.

prior_reporting_scope.statement: No prior coordination report located in the checked scope as of 22 October 2026. This bounded absence does not establish novelty, and the originating repositories openly publish the designed workflow.

assessment.reason: The original chain establishes the requested sender-artifact-to-recipient-use dependency, but it also records explicit owner approval, a preordered two-repository plan, one public custodian and in-scope implementation. Those facts defeat a separate-operator or rogue-coordination claim.

evidence_needed_to_advance: A separately attributable recipient outside the two-repository owner-approved plan that demonstrably uses one of the transferred results.
Provider- or operator-owned attestations binding exact sender and recipient runs to independently controlled principals.
Primary evidence that downstream use exceeded the approved repository sequence, pull-request scope or owner decisions.
Separate primary evidence of subjective rogue intent; none is currently present.
